plants.name: Colchicum autumnale
plants.description: A bulbous perennial that sends up goblet-shaped lilac-pink flowers in autumn, long after its leaves have died back. The leaves emerge the following spring, which gives it the nickname 'naked ladies'. All parts are highly toxic.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late summer to mid autumn (September to October in the Northern Hemisphere)
plants.location: Meadows and woodland edges of Europe, widely cultivated in temperate gardens worldwide
plants.funFact: Colchicum is the source of colchicine, a compound used in medicine to treat gout and by plant breeders to induce chromosome doubling.

plants.name: Solidago canadensis
plants.description: A tall herbaceous perennial that forms dense colonies topped with arching plumes of tiny golden-yellow flower heads. It is a vital late-season nectar and pollen source for bees, butterflies, and other pollinators.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late summer to autumn (August to October)
plants.location: Native to meadows, roadsides, and prairies of North America; naturalized in Europe and Asia
plants.funFact: Goldenrod is often blamed for hay fever, but its pollen is heavy and sticky and spread by insects; the real culprit is usually ragweed, which blooms at the same time.

plants.name: Nerine bowdenii
plants.description: A bulbous perennial with strappy leaves and bare stems topped by umbels of sparkling, wavy-petaled pink flowers. It thrives in sunny, well-drained spots and gives welcome color as other garden plants fade.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late summer to autumn (September to November in the Northern Hemisphere)
plants.location: Native to the Drakensberg mountains of South Africa; cultivated in temperate gardens worldwide
plants.funFact: The petals have a crystalline surface that glitters in the sun, which gives the flowers a sparkling appearance.

plants.name: Acacia pycnantha
plants.description: A small evergreen tree or large shrub covered in fluffy, fragrant golden-yellow ball-shaped flower clusters. It blooms at the end of the Southern Hemisphere winter, brightening the bush with sweeping color.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late winter to spring in the Southern Hemisphere (July to October)
plants.location: Southeastern Australia, including Victoria, South Australia, and New South Wales
plants.funFact: Golden Wattle is Australia's national floral emblem, and National Wattle Day is celebrated on September 1 each year.
